properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-30, on seeing past release mistakes surface again at each cut: *"I'm not sure where these lessons learned are stored (in the agent's memory or in a .md file somewhere or maybe they are in the reflow2 graph like I want them to be)."*

═══ FACET 1: THEY ARE IN THE GRAPH — IN THREE PLACES, WITH NO ONE VIEW ═══

Answered by looking, 2026-08-30. The release lessons are recorded, and they are DesignRules, a Flow, and TemporalFacts:

· `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` — from the v0.38.0 manifest that shipped empty because a dry run reads like a write.
· `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch`, `rule:a-gate-is-run-against-the-state-it-will-be-judged-in`, `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly`, `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed`.
· `flow:release-cut` — the procedure itself, with `cap:a-cut-is-read-from-the-design`: *"a cut is read from the design rather than from the last one."*
· `fact:three-shipping-mistakes-the-gates-caught-and-one-they-did-not`, `fact:export-must-be-last-means-last-relative-to-main-not-to-the-branch`.

⭐ SO THE ANSWER TO HIS QUESTION IS "YES, MOSTLY" — and the gap is not capture, it is that a LESSON HAS NO SINGLE HOME OR VIEW. Three node types hold them by different routes, and which one a given lesson landed in depends on the session that wrote it rather than on what kind of lesson it is. `fact:todays-gate-lessons-have-a-served-home-and-it-is-empty` (2026-08-14) says a version of this already.

🛑 AND ONE PART IS GENUINELY OUTSIDE THE GRAPH, WHICH IS THE HALF HE FEARED. Some release knowledge lives in the AGENT'S OWN MEMORY FILES, which are not the design, not visible to him, and not visible to any other contributor or agent. One such note asserts the seven release steps *"exist nowhere else as a list"* — while `flow:release-cut` exists. Either the note is stale or the Flow is incomplete, and NOTHING CAN TELL WHICH, because the two records cannot see each other. A lesson in agent memory is a lesson the project does not have.

═══ FACET 2: A USER CANNOT SAY "GET THE PERMIT FIRST" ═══

His example: *"on my brother's garage design, maybe there is something in the graph that says, before building, must obtain permit from city for XYZ."*

Measured: the vocabulary for this is DECLARED AND EMPTY — QualityGate 0 instances, EnvironmentRule 0, GATED_ON 0 edges (see dec:idea-the-governance-layer-is-declared-and-mostly-unused).

⭐ AND `GATED_ON` IS THE WRONG SHAPE ANYWAY, WHICH IS THE SHARPER FINDING. It carries a READINESS RUNG — `kind` TRL or MRL, `min_level` 1-9. It says "this increment needs that technology at TRL 6." A permit is not a rung. It is a PRECONDITION WITH AN AUTHORITY AND A DATE: somebody external grants it, it is obtained or it is not, and there is no level 4 of having a permit. Same shape for an inspection, a certification, a sign-off, a landlord's consent, a change-control board approval — and for the GitLab push rules Anthony mentions his brother's employer having.

So reflow2 can express "wait until this is mature enough" and cannot express "wait until someone else has said yes." Those are different, and only the first is built.

📌 IT CONNECTS TO WHAT WAS ACCEPTED TODAY. `req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off` says the agent must not author artifacts carrying professional accountability. A permit is exactly such an artifact — so the design already has a rule ABOUT these things while having no way to MODEL one.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) A LESSON IS ITS OWN THING, with one home and one view, whatever produced it.
(b) LESSONS STAY WHERE THEY ARE and a VIEW gathers them — cheaper, changes no vocabulary, and matches "views are projections".
(c) A PRECONDITION BECOMES EXPRESSIBLE — an obligation with an authority, a status and a date, distinct from a readiness rung. New vocabulary, and `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` demands something read it before it is added.
(d) STOP PUTTING PROJECT KNOWLEDGE IN AGENT MEMORY, or at least detect the split. Independent of the rest and the only one that costs nothing.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether (c) is one new concept or three (permit, approval, certification), and whether a Verification with an external provenance already covers most of it. Nobody has tried.
properties.name: OPEN — the release lessons ARE in the graph, scattered across three node types; and a user cannot yet say "get the permit before you build"
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill while the current increment stays the priority. Split from the vocabulary-usage node because these are different questions: that one asks whether the governance layer earns its keep, this asks where a lesson belongs and what shape a precondition is. The first facet turned out to be answerable by looking, so it is recorded as an answer with its remaining gap rather than as an open question.
